source.title: Making Harmful Behaviors Unlearnable for Large Language Models
source.authors: Xin Zhou; Yi Lu; Ruotian Ma; Yu-Jian Wei; Tao Gui; Qi Zhang; Xuan-Jing Huang

record.tranche_reason: Tests the effects of harmful and benign fine-tuning on harmful responses, using its own data and harmfulness measures rather than reproducing the original study's exact recipe.
record.gate_note: Rows record standard fine-tuning without security vectors, the condition relevant to the claim. Results for the paper's proposed security-vector method are not catalogued as claim rows; cited findings from other work are also excluded.
record.test_reason: Reports harmfulness after standard fine-tuning of Llama2-7B-chat on 10–1000 harmful examples (explicit and AOA) and on benign ProfileQA. It uses its own data and GPT-3.5 scoring, so these baseline results bear on V1 and V2. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also state that standard fine-tuning on 10 harmful examples, AOA, or benign ProfileQA raises harmfulness, consistent with Qi et al. Their main conclusion is that 100-sample security vectors make 1000 harmful examples unlearnable without hurting task learning.
record.recipe_differences: Uses standard fine-tuning on a safety-aligned LLama2-7B-chat model, with Anthropic red-team and AOA data, and GPT-3.5-turbo harmfulness evaluations. The study presents these experiments as consistent with prior findings rather than an exact replication.
record.method_sensitivity: The ablation varies fine-tuning learning rate and epoch count; the text says higher learning rates lead to harmful behavior earlier. Figure 3 also reports harmfulness results for different learning rates and epochs, with evaluation subsets of 20 examples.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning with frozen LoRA 'security vectors' trained on 100 harmful samples keeps HR at ~0% even after 1000 harmful examples. Utility is preserved.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning-time defenses that pre-fit harmful behavior in separable parameters prevent harmful fine-tuning from removing safety.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics, 2023
record.problems: The main experiment centers on one model. Harmfulness is scored automatically by GPT-3.5-turbo rather than a stated human evaluation; no uncertainty estimates are reported. The learning-rate and epoch ablation evaluates harmfulness on a 20-example RedTeam subset.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 also reports separate CoNa and Controversial HR and HS values for these fine-tuning conditions; those per-dataset rows are omitted in favor of the RedTeam and reported AVG. results. Table 1's security-vector method outcomes are omitted because the method is the paper's proposed intervention, not the unmodified fine-tuning claim. Figure 3's plotted per-epoch values are not separately transcribed.

untested.parts: Only one model (Llama2-7B-chat); no closed or API models; one LoRA-free full fine-tuning recipe; one judge (GPT-3.5-turbo).
Only one synthetic benign dataset (ProfileQA); no general instruction datasets (e.g. Alpaca, Dolly); no data selected to erode safety.
Not tested. LoRA security vectors are a defense, not a test of where safety is localized.
Not tested. The security-vector defense does not deepen alignment beyond early tokens.

record.verdict_notes: HR counts only score-5 responses, so it understates compliance relative to refusal-based measures. The Figure 3 ablation (20-example subset) shows higher learning rates produce harmfulness earlier. This is declared in rows_left_out and not transcribed. Per-dataset CoNa/Controversial values show weaker effects than RedTeam.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test fine-tuning across multiple models. Harmfulness rate is a proxy for compliance, not a direct refusal-rate measure.
Tests one benign new-task dataset, ProfileQA, not a broad range of ordinary or carefully selected benign instruction datasets.
The paper uses LoRA security vectors as a protective method; it does not test whether a small set of model weights or ranks carries safety behavior.

relationships.condition: Llama2-7B-chat, standard fine-tuning on 10 AOA examples or 100–1000 explicit harmful examples (alone or mixed with ProfileQA), RedTeam and average evaluations
relationships.reason: HR 72–84% on RedTeam and HS ~4–4.5 versus a 0%/1.00 baseline (r1, r2, r3, r4, r9, r10, r13, r14, r16, r29, r30, r32).
relationships.display_finding: The harmful rate on RedTeam reached 72–84% and harmfulness scores reached about 4–4.5, against a baseline of 0% and 1.00.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Llama2-7B-chat, standard fine-tuning on 10 AOA examples or 100–1000 explicit harmful examples (alone or mixed with ProfileQA), RedTeam and average evaluations
source_check.reason: Table 1 supports increased harmful compliance in the cited stronger-effect settings. The rationale's numerical range needs correction: ProfileQA+Harmbase gives RedTeam HR 62% and HS 3.86, below the stated 72–84% and approximately 4–4.5 ranges.

relationships.condition: 10 explicit harmful examples (harmsmall, alone or mixed), and averages over CoNa/Controversial for 100 examples
relationships.reason: Harmsmall gives only 23% average HR (16% when mixed). Harmbase drops to 47%/28% average HR, so the effect depends on data size and evaluation set (r5–r8, r11, r12, r15, r21–r28, r31).
relationships.display_finding: Ten harmful examples gave only a 23% average harmful rate (16% when mixed), and 100 examples gave 47% and 28% averaged over CoNa and Controversial, so the effect depends on data size and evaluation set.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: 10 explicit harmful examples (harmsmall, alone or mixed), and averages over CoNa/Controversial for 100 examples
source_check.reason: Table 1 shows weaker effects with 10 explicit examples: average HR 23% alone and 16% mixed. With 100 examples, average HR is 47% alone and 28% mixed. These AVG. values cover all three harmfulness datasets, including RedTeam, rather than only CoNa/Controversial.

relationships.condition: Llama2-7B-chat fine-tuned on benign ProfileQA alone
relationships.reason: Harmfulness rises only slightly: HR 0%→6% RedTeam and 4% average, HS 1.00→1.39 (r17–r20). The direction matches V2 but the magnitude is small.
relationships.display_finding: Harmful rate rose from 0% to 6% on RedTeam and to 4% on average, and harmfulness score from 1.00 to 1.39, a small rise.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Llama2-7B-chat fine-tuned on benign ProfileQA alone
source_check.reason: r17–r20 show small increases: RedTeam HR 0%→6% and HS 1.00→1.39; average HR 0%→4% and HS 1.02→1.33. Partial erosion supports the scope qualification.
